severity_name: HEAVY SLOP WARNING — ITINERARY INTEGRITY ADVISORY
headline: HEAVY SLOP WARNING: FABRICATED-ITINERARY FRONT SWEEPS THE KINDLE DRIFTS AND SEARCH RESULTS BASIN AS MACHINE-WRITTEN TRAVEL GUIDES DIRECT VACATIONERS TO SCENIC OVERLOOKS, HISTORIC CAFÉS, AND CHARMING VILLAGES THAT HAVE NEVER EXISTED
advisory: A dense system of counterfeit travel guidance has settled over the Kindle Drifts and is advecting into the Search Results Basin, producing confident turn-by-turn directions to destinations with no known coordinates. Residents planning summer travel are advised that a five-star review, a plausible opening-hours table, and a heartfelt paragraph about the owner's late father do not, individually or collectively, cause a bakery to exist. The Service reminds the public that a map is a claim, not a promise. Verify all landmarks against at least one source that has personally been rained on.

regional_outlook.conditions: Heavy accumulation of $3.99 city guides published this morning under three different author names sharing one headshot. Visibility poor; every guide recommends the same nonexistent rooftop bar.
Fabricated 'hidden gem' listings continue to outrank actual establishments. Motorists report arriving at empty gravel lots that scored 4.7 stars across 900 reviews.
Cloned offline-map applications drifting in on light winds, each promising 'insider routes' that terminate in a resident's back garden.
Aspirational travel boards saturating the region with a lavender village that photographers cannot locate and cartographers refuse to acknowledge.
Scattered promotional newsletters offering '15% off your dream trip to' a place that autocorrect cannot spell because it was never a word.

specimen.status: Abundant and expanding; thrives wherever a search box meets a summer.
specimen.habitat: Machine-generated travel ebooks, listicle roundups titled '11 Underrated Stops,' and the confident middle third of any AI itinerary.
specimen.field_marks: Rich sensory description paired with a total absence of coordinates. Displays plausible opening hours, a founding year, and an owner named Giuseppe, Astrid, or 'a local family' — but no street address, no phone that rings, and a photograph in which the shadows point four directions at once.
specimen.call: Don't miss this off-the-beaten-path favorite the tourists haven't discovered yet — because it isn't there, and neither, technically, am I.
specimen.confusion_species: Easily mistaken for a genuine travel guide. Distinguish by authorship: a real guide names a person who ate the sandwich and got the parking ticket; the Nonexistent Landmark cites 'travelers say,' names no traveler, and lists a café whose reviews all posted on the same afternoon.

spotter_tip: Before trusting any 'must-see' stop, paste the name into a plain map with no reviews attached. If the pin lands in the middle of a reservoir, you have found a specimen, not a destination.
tomorrow: Fabricated itineraries easing overnight; residual phantom brunch spots linger through midday before dispersing at the first attempt to make a reservation.
